subject: Renewal: commit sizing, per-token bands, and rollover guardrails
messages:
From: Priyanka Desai <p.desai@beaconcare.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: BeaconCare Procurement <procurement@beaconcare.com>
Date: 2026-11-29 15:04 -0800
Subject: Renewal: commit sizing and per-token bands

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off our renewal conversations for our hosted API usage. Over the past 12 months our footprint has skewed towards bursty inference (short-lived spikes tied to weekly campaigns) and our Q3 run-rate ended up ~30% below the commit level in the current contract.

Before we get into paperwork, procurement asked if Redwood can consider:
- a smaller baseline commit for next year with a 90-day true-up vs fixed quarterly true-up
- per-token discount tiers that don't penalize short-term spikes (we saw a per-token cliff in the last renewal)
- a hard uplift cap year-over-year so our finance team can budget (ideally max 15–20%)

Can you share a proposal that preserves a meaningful discount at scale but gives us a safety valve for burst months? I've attached a Q3 usage extract.

Thanks,
Priyanka
Priyanka Desai
Head of Procurement, BeaconCare
procurement@beaconcare.com

Attachment: BeaconCare_usage_report_Q3.csv (csv, 87KB)

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Desai <p.desai@beaconcare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30 09:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: commit sizing and per-token bands

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear note and the usage extract. Appreciate the signal on predictability needs.

High-level proposal attached — two paths we typically offer for customers with bursty patterns:

Option A — Right-sized commit + conservative discount curve
- Baseline commit = historical 6‑month rolling median * 1.05
- Per-token discount tiers that smooth between 0–1B tokens to avoid cliffs (see table in term sheet)
- 90‑day rolling true-up, no quarterly reconciliation penalty
- Rollover credits: unused commit up to 25% can roll into the next quarter once per year

Option B — Lower commit + flexible uplifts
- Baseline commit = historical 3‑month median * 1.0
- Higher per-token price on first band, deeper discounts past 1B tokens to incentivize scale
- 90‑day true-up + automatic 30% burst protection (protects against a single-month spike)

We can bake in an explicit annual uplift cap. Finance-friendly caps we've accepted recently are 15% (preferred) or 20% (upper). If you prefer, we can add a staircase that allows a one-time administrative increase during the year for predictable campaign-driven growth.

Attached: BeaconCare_Renewal_Termsheet_v2.pdf — includes sample pricing tables, the proposed true-up cadence, and a clause for rollover credits.

Next steps: please confirm which option (A/B) you want to model and whether procurement needs any additional evidence (SOC 2, audit logs) on the contract before legal reviews.

Best,
So Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Attachment: BeaconCare_Renewal_Termsheet_v2.pdf (pdf, 142KB)

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01 10:03 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: commit sizing and per-token bands

Looping you both in — Priyanka is leaning toward Option A but asked about a hard uplift cap. Key asks from procurement:
- 90-day true-up (OK per sheet)
- hard uplift cap target 15% (they said 15–20%)
- smoother per-token curve with no cliff in the first band

Can we accept 15% as the standard uplift cap for this ARR band? Also, thoughts on the rollover credit mechanics (25% cap, once per year) vs allowing prorated carry-forward?

Quick replies appreciated — procurement is on a tight calendar.

— Soojin

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05 14:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: commit sizing and per-token bands

Thanks for the context. My take:
- 15% hard uplift cap is acceptable for this account if we pair it with a modestly higher baseline (Option A approach) so Redwood isn't exposed to sustained under-commit risk.
- Approve the 90-day true-up and the 25% annual rollover credit, but change rollover to apply only against the following quarter (not the full year) — keeps runway predictable.
- Pricing cliff fix: agree to smooth the first two bands. Use continuous breakpoints at 250M and 1B tokens (rather than abrupt jumps).

Operational asks for legal/ops: we should add an explicit clause that automatic fallback to hosted standard rates happens only after a 30‑day cure period following reconciliation. Also please attach the SOC 2 evidence link to the terms.

I'll greenlight this to be sent to procurement once Soojin updates the sheet with the baseline delta and the change to rollover timing.

-rishi

From: Priyanka Desai <p.desai@beaconcare.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: BeaconCare Procurement <procurement@beaconcare.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@docusignpro.com>
Date: 2026-12-14 09:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: commit sizing and per-token bands

Thanks Soojin and team — this is helpful. We reviewed the updated term sheet and the changes from Rishi look reasonable. A couple of outstanding items from procurement:

1) Please add the SOC 2 attestations link into the contract appendix (we'll need it for our audit).
2) We want the 15% annual uplift cap as a hard cap in the billing schedule.
3) Confirm the rollover credit applies only to the immediately following quarter (per Rishi's note).
4) DocuSign: can you send the updated term sheet via DocuSign once legal inserts the SOC 2 link? Aaron (cc'd) can assist with embedded signing.

If you can get the DocuSign envelope out this week, procurement will target signature by 12/28.

Thanks,
Priyanka
